title: QuantaMed POC scoping - open models
summary: POC scoping for Triaged clinical QA and note summarization. Key success criteria: clinical accuracy on labeled set, PII handling and data residency, latency SLO ~ <350ms for 256-token responses, and cost targets. Shortlist of open models (Llama 3 variants, Mistral 8x, Falcon 40B) with tradeoffs discussed. Timeline: 3-4 week POC, benchmarks in week 2, security review parallel. Next steps: Redwood to share benchmark plan + pricing, QuantaMed to share sample dataset and SOC2 questionnaire.
next_steps: Redwood: send POC benchmark plan and sample infra template (by 2026-07-10)
QuantaMed: share 500-1k de-identified clinical examples and PI extraction spec (by 2026-07-12)
Schedule benchmark run week of 2026-07-20 (Redwood + QuantaMed)
Follow-up call to review results week of 2026-07-27
action_items: Maya Chen: prepare benchmark config and cost estimate (due 2026-07-10)
Daniel Ortiz: prepare test harness and end-to-end latency script (due 2026-07-12)
Samir Patel: provide de-identified sample corpus and label schema (due 2026-07-12)
Dr. Clara Nguyen: sign and return SOC2 questionnaire (due 2026-07-15)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to kick off the poc scoping for quanta med. quick intros?
[00:06] Dr. Clara Nguyen: hi i'm clara head of data at quanta med, we own the clinical qa and summarization workstreams.
[00:11] Samir Patel: samir here, ml eng, i'll be hands-on with the tests and infra.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: lena product, i'll be owning success criteria and stakeholder alignment.
[00:19] Maya Chen: great. daniel from our infra team?
[00:21] Daniel Ortiz: yep hi all, se focused on benchmarks and private deployments.
[00:25] Maya Chen: ok quick agenda, set success criteria, size the workload, pick model shortlist, discuss security and timelines.
[00:33] Dr. Clara Nguyen: for success we need clinically accurate answers for triage questions — precision on critical labels > 92% ideally, and false negatives low. also need pii redaction and residency in us-eu.
[00:44] Lena Ortiz: and product metric is time-to-insight: end user should get summaries < 1s ideally, but we know that's tight.
[00:51] Daniel Ortiz: to unpack latency we usually split into model infer time + network + pre/post processing. for a 256-token response we can target model tail latency ~200-300ms on a dedicated GPU and end-to-end ~350-500ms depending on infra.
[01:05] Samir Patel: our expected volume for the POC is low — maybe 5-10 qps peak, but production could be 40-60 qps. cost is a hard constraint, so we'll look at quantized model options.
[01:16] Maya Chen: good, that aligns with typical poc sizing. for the shortlist we usually test 3-4 open models to compare quality/cost. daniel what are you recommending given medical language and some spanish/french notes?
[01:27] Daniel Ortiz: i'd suggest Llama-3 13B (quantized), Mistral 8x or Mistral-instruct variant, and Falcon 40B for a higher-quality baseline. there's also variants of Llama-3 70B but that's heavier and more costly. for multilingual i'd add a mpt/mistral family that's good on european languages — though performance on medical vernacular varies.
[01:45] Dr. Clara Nguyen: curious — how often do you see Llama-3 outperfom medic-specific models? transcription: llma-3, sorry.
[01:51] Daniel Ortiz: yeah, model names get mangled in transcription, but in practice Llama-3 13B fine-tuned or instruction-tuned can do well on structured QA with prompt engineering. falcon 40b tends to give more fluent long-form summarization but can hallucinate on rare medical facts. Mistral 8x is a strong cost/quality sweet spot in our benchmarks.
[02:05] Maya Chen: important tradeoffs: latency/cost vs Knowledge fidelity. for clinical accuracy we recommend running an eval set of ~500 labeled questions covering edge cases — we'll compute EM/precision/recall and a medical-specific F1.
[02:17] Samir Patel: we have about ~2k de-identified notes and could surface 500 examples. we'll need guidance on de-id process.
[02:22] Lena Ortiz: also want to check hallucination rates and calibration — false confident wrong answers are a dealbreaker.
[02:30] Daniel Ortiz: for hallucination detection we'll use a combination of model confidence scoring and reference comparisons. we can instrument per-token logprobs and produce a hallucination metric.
[02:38] Maya Chen: security — QuantaMed mentioned residency. we support Private deployment (VPC) and dedicated pools. do you expect to run this POC in hosted or private?
[02:46] Dr. Clara Nguyen: prefer private (VPC) for the POC to validate network flows and kms integration — we need KMS/HSM for keys and SOC2 controls.
[02:53] Daniel Ortiz: that's fine. we can provision a private POC cluster with customer-managed VPC peering and KMS integration. for initial bench runs we sometimes do a short hosted run to iterate faster then switch to private for final benchmarks.
[03:05] Lena Ortiz: timeline question — how long to get benchmarks back?
[03:08] Maya Chen: typical is 2-3 weeks end-to-end: week 1 data & infra setup, week 2 benchmark runs and initial results, week 3 follow-ups and remediation. so 3-4 week POC is realistic.
[03:18] Daniel Ortiz: lab details — we'll test single-request latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput with the expected batch sizes, and quality on the labeled set. we'll run quantized 4-bit variants where applicable and compare to fp16 if needed.
[03:30] Samir Patel: do you have sample numbers we can expect for cost vs latency?
[03:33] Daniel Ortiz: rough ballpark from similar workloads: Llama-3 13B quantized on a T4-equivalent or A10-equivalent gives ~200-300ms median and lower token cost; Mistral 8x often matches or beats that at lower cost; Falcon 40B fp16 will be 2-3x cost and lower latency variance on beefy GPUs but more expensive. we'll provide a precise estimate in the benchmark plan.
[03:50] Dr. Clara Nguyen: multilingual — about 15% of notes are spanish, 5% french, many with clinical shorthand. do any models handle that mix natively?
[03:58] Daniel Ortiz: Mistral and some Llama variants do reasonably well with europeans languages. we may recommend a small fine-tune or retrieval-augmented prompts for critical span detection in spanish. embedding models for semantic search need to be checked too — we can test multiling embeddings (we have a redwood-verified set).
[04:11] Maya Chen: retrieval isn't the main POC focus, but we can include a quick RAG bench to see if grounding reduces hallucination.
[04:16] Lena Ortiz: regulatory question: audit logs and traceability — we need request-level audit logs for compliance.
[04:21] Daniel Ortiz: Redwood Console supports per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, and audit logs exportable to your SIEM. we also support RBAC and SSO integrations.
[04:30] Samir Patel: for the POC do we need a contract?
[04:33] Maya Chen: we usually do a short POC agreement for dedicated resources and SLA, but for small POCs we can do a scoped trial under standard terms. we'll have sales send pricing.
[04:41] Dr. Clara Nguyen: what's the worst-case for data exfil? i.e., model training on customer data?
[04:46] Daniel Ortiz: we don't use customer data for model training. in private and dedicated modes data stays in your VPC or dedicated pool and isn't added to public training sets. we'll include the data handling section in the security docs.
[04:56] Maya Chen: ok recap: QuantaMed will share de-identified corpus and label schema; Redwood will deliver benchmark plan, infra template, and cost estimate; we'll run bench week of 7/20 and reconvene week of 7/27 to review.
[05:08] Lena Ortiz: sounds good, thanks.
[05:10] Maya Chen: I'll send notes, docs and next steps. thanks everyone.
notes: Redwood to provide benchmark plan with exact GPU sizing and quantization recipes
